The browser add-on is still running the old version
Crow updated the browser add-on, but the copy that is running is still the old one. Restart it to load the update. A restart cannot be undone, and the pages that are open in the browser now will close. Saved logins and cookies are kept.
Open Extensions
AI Companion was retired
AI Companion is no longer part of Crow, but it is still installed on this Crow. Press "Remove it": Crow runs its own uninstall path and keeps the add-on's data folder (your conversations, models and settings stay there). There is no undo beyond that.
Audiobookshelf is still published to other devices
Audiobookshelf is published to other devices; Crow now ships it on this computer only. Restart won't change that while its settings file has local changes — see the other card.
Open Extensions
Vikunja's settings file has an update Crow did not apply
Crow keeps Vikunja on its current settings because the update would also change its image (vikunja/vikunja:0.24.6 → vikunja/vikunja:0.25.1; it may be older than what is running). The update also tightens how Vikunja is published. Back up its data, then press 'Apply the update' to switch, or keep it as it is.

Vikunja's settings file was not updated
Crow could not update Vikunja's settings file: it needs VIKUNJA_DB_PASSWORD set first (Configure on its Extensions card).
Open Extensions
Changedetection.io's settings file has local changes
Changedetection.io's settings file (docker-compose.yml) has local changes, so Crow did not update it. Move your changes into docker-compose.override.yml and restore the settings file (a copy of the current one is kept as docker-compose.yml.bak when Crow restores it).
Open Extensions
Restart Audiobookshelf to apply its updated network settings
Audiobookshelf is still reachable on 0.0.0.0:13378 from other devices, but its settings now keep it on this computer only. Restart it on the Extensions page to apply them.

The boot guard did not run ×2
This service is configured to roll back a Crow update that keeps crashing on startup (CROW_BOOT_GUARD=1), but the part that runs before every start did not run. Re-run the boot-guard install step for this service, then restart it.
This machine's Caddy admin API is open to any program on it
Caddy's admin API is on its default local address with no authentication, so any program or bot on this machine can rewrite the Caddy that fronts Crow. Crow does not run as root, so run this once on the server: sudo bash /srv/crow/scripts/fix-caddy-admin-socket.sh

Visitors coming in through this machine's Caddy are being turned away
Caddy still hands them to the gateway over a loopback connection with its own forwarding header, which Crow cannot tell apart from any other program on this machine — so Crow's Nest refuses them. Crow does not run as root, so run this once on the server: sudo bash /srv/crow/scripts/fix-caddy-proxy-socket.sh
